sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Apparel growth is real in reported accounts, but not yet cash-realized: FY26 revenue250.7865cr and PAT18.0887cr coexist with CFO−40.0014cr. At the dated secondary97.80 close, a linked base scenario produces only2.68% annual return before execution costs, while requiring additional funding. This is a conditional diagnostic, not a reliable point forecast. [S1] [S2] [S95]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Bizotic Commercial Limited, BSE543926/BIZOTIC, ISIN INE0OJ401014, BSE SME. Standalone Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, year ended31March2026; research as of20October2026. Five-year synthetic model,15% return hurdle and₹5lakh liquidity reference. EGM23October is future; no proposal is treated as approved. [S1] [S3]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Urban United and Yard apparel trading/distribution, not a manufacturing-capacity story. Chairman reports16 outlets; IPO-era21 included4owned/17franchised, so definitions/dates must be reconciled before declaring growth or contraction in comparable stores. Purchases of traded goods dominate cost; credit terms, inventory selection and retailer sell-through drive economic success. [S1] [S4]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Brands and distribution create ordinary differentiation, but no independently demonstrated durable premium or switching cost. Current gross margin about13.65% versus12.05% last year is encouraging, not proof of moat. Prospectus peers Trent, BellaCasa and Lorenzini differ materially in model/scale; its February2023 prices and pre-bonus EPS units cannot support a current peer multiple. [S1] [S4] [S6]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Sales grew from65.1573cr inFY23 to71.426cr inFY24,111.9468cr inFY25 and250.7865cr inFY26. FY26+124.0% growth is accompanied by receivables rising from24.4841cr to89.7663cr. Historical IPO concentration was80.05% in top10 customers for nine monthsDecember2022, with120-day credit; this is a dated risk indicator, not a current customer statistic. [S1] [S4] [S5] [S6]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Expansion is working-capital-intensive. Inventory75.285cr, supplier advances17.2321cr and receivables89.7663cr exceed the comfort suggested by8.1264cr financial debt. September proposes149.688cr entirely for working capital; price110 is above the dated97.8 close, making full exercise uncertain. Growth financed repeatedly by equity is not automatically per-share compounding. [S1] [S3] [S95]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
DGMS resigned25October2024 for preoccupation, explicitly denying management disputes and information suppression. J Singh resigned19December2025; separate letter not recovered, but current CARO says outgoing auditor raised no issues. Shweta Jain replaced it; CFO/CS turnover adds execution risk, not proof of wrongdoing. Audit trail was not operated throughoutFY25/FY26. AOC-2 discloses promoter loan repayment10.4826cr and related subscriptions; February corrigendum names Sangita Aggarwala/Sanjay Gupta as beneficial owners of corporate allottees. These disclosed flows require reconciliation, not automatic reassurance or accusation. [S1] [S6] [S7] [S8]

Signed printedpage115 corrects the AOC-2 narrative ambiguity: Sangita loan taken13.4482cr less repaid10.4826cr plus opening3.1178cr equals closing6.0834cr. Warrant issuance to Sangita is7.3080cr, not13.4482cr. Corporate warrant rows5.8+6.728+9.976+8.99cr plus7.308cr total38.802cr, and Nexus pending1.914cr reconciles total40.716cr financing cash. This resolves rather than compounds the earlier related-subscription discrepancy. MohitHUF franchise deposit.4cr is disclosed; Amanjeet supplier advance.0811cr closes from.0386+.0425. MD loan given.135cr plus opening.0035cr and repayment.1385cr closes nil. These related transactions are disclosed flows, not proof of diversion. [S1] [S8]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 working-capital movement−59.7908cr plus operating cash profit26.1921cr less tax6.4027cr equals CFO−40.0014cr: the subtotal is mislabeled, final arithmetic reconciles. Receivables65.2822cr, stock23.5357cr and advances13.4489cr absorbed cash; payables50.0683cr partly funded it, while other liabilities fell14.018cr. Cash PPE4.8585cr gives FCF−44.8599cr. The following normalization and capital bridge separates reported results from unquantified balance/provision uncertainty. [S1] [S2]

Restated FY20/FY21/FY22 sales11.1364/16.7995/53.4139cr, PAT.1634/.3408/.5957cr and CFO−2.8528/−2.0041/−1.3215cr. FY23 PAT2.6897cr/CFO−3.0842cr; FY24 PAT3.0838cr/CFOoriginal−26.0849cr versus−25.1827cr in next annual comparative, approximately.9023cr interest classification difference. Both remain deeply negative. FY24 other income4.5943cr exceeded PBT4.0314cr, including writeback2.0215cr, capital gains1.1882cr, interest.9023cr and speculative/intraday gains. FY25 F&O loss.9943cr disappears inFY26; do not attribute its removal to improved merchandise margins. FY26 core EBIT=PBT24.926+.1804finance−.1219other income=24.9845cr. FY25 core6.2898cr or7.2841cr excluding F&O loss. At assumed25% tax, current NOPAT18.7384cr versus4.7174–5.4631cr. Equity including1.914cr pending subscriptions+debt−cash capital121.1206cr versus60.634cr produces20.62% average and21.95–23.18% incremental return. This CWIP/all-capital-inclusive proxy does not validate receivable recoverability. [S1] [S2] [S4] [S5] [S6]

Long-term advances13.6098cr are security deposits, not assumed director loans. Current supplier advances17.2321cr rose from2.8991cr. Customer advances fell13.0501cr to.1181cr and security deposits received3.583cr to1.3925cr, explaining part of cash absorption. Cash3.863cr includes1.0431cr physical cash; bank2.8199cr is not the whole cash balance. Receivables are classified good without doubtful provision, but the ageing table places89.7663cr against a poorly aligned heading; no unsupported age bucket is assigned. Auditor reports management inventory verification/most third-party confirmations and no loan default. These are counterevidence, not independent proof of collections. Persistent edit-log exception limits traceability. [S1]

Printed page112 notes27–30 materially qualify reliance on otherwise unmodified accounts. Note27 says unsecured loans, payables, debtors and advances remain subject to confirmation and profit impact cannot be ascertained. Note28 says director unsecured lending lacks written agreement. Note29 states gratuity is recognized when claimed rather than actuarially valued underAS15, with unquantified effect; note30 contains contradictory wording about PF/ESIC compliance and true/fair result, requiring clarification rather than assuming a statutory default. These are source disclosures, not an allegation of manipulation. They make the recovery and capital-return inputs insufficiently reliable for investment ranking. CARO also prints GST appeal tables despite a generic no-disputed-dues sentence; do not treat that boilerplate as clearance. [S1]

Financial note49 (printedpage120) discloses GST appeals22.37lakh and58.51lakh, total80.88lakh (0.8088cr), versus different amounts in the CARO table. Use0.8088cr as the signed-note disclosed contingent amount, not as a settled liability or legal outcome. The generic no-disputed-dues sentence does not override the specific table; obtain reconciliation. [S1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Primary September capitalization57.852million shares matches active official lot1200 and yields565.79256cr market cap at secondary19October97.8. Historical FY26 PAT implies31.28× using current shares, not an undated cheap multiple. Linked scenarios include annual taxes, NWC, capex, debt, interest and cash; proposed warrants are modeled only in separate conditional fully-funded alternatives. No numeric IAS because funding and recovery assumptions remain low confidence. [S1] [S3] [S91] [S95]

March shares9.378million plusApril conversion.264million become9.642million; subsequent5:1 bonus gives57.852million, independently confirmed inSeptember notice. Remaining April75% subscription5.742cr is added only to a proforma March cash bridge, not asserted as October cash. New proposed13.608million warrants@110 would raise149.688cr gross and increase shares to71.460million.25%potential37.422cr is not full funding. Alternative model assumes complete conversion upfront,2%issue costs and146.69424cr net; this favorable counterfactual is explicitly separate from present capital. Allotee approvals, actual receipt and conversion must be distinguished. [S1] [S3] [S8]

Current-capital bear/base/bull terminal prices7.85/109.60/229.20 imply five-year returns−39.62%/+2.30%/+18.57%;15%hurdle entries3.90/54.49/114.82. Peak debt76.83/23.06/11.37cr and total new borrowing73.98/14.93/0cr expose financing dependencies. Full proposed-warrant counterfactual terminal30.86/110.12/206.34 yields-20.60%/+2.40%/+16.10%; cash benefit and dilution are both included, unused cash retained rather than spent twice. Base margin10% approximates current coreEBIT margin, but NWC gradually improving43%→40% still requires proof; bear65% captures credit stress, bull30%is optimistic release. Two-way exit multiple/discount and hurdle grids accompany the annual bridge. At15%hurdle, terminal share price196.71 needs75.87cr PAT at15×PE oncurrent shares, about4.19×FY26; new full shares increase this requirement to93.71cr before considering cash proceeds. [S1] [S3] [S95]

Secondary19October price97.8, volume150000, low94.55/high99.9 implies price×volume bounds14.1825–14.985million rupees, not official turnover. Active officialSM lot1200 costs117360rupees; four lots469440 approximate but do not equal the5lakh reference. Provider history appears price-adjusted around5:1bonus; volume adjustment is unverified, so60-session turnover is excluded. Entirely post-bonus20-session low×volume proxy mean4.533654million/median4.101630million gives theoretical5lakh exits6.095/2.438/1.219days at2/5/10%participation. All20 rows observed, but this is a proxy window, not required verified60-day traded value. No spread/depth/BSE surveillance clearance; L remains NS rather than converting proxy into an execution score. [S3] [S91] [S95]

Research-model correction, 20 October 2026: the earlier scenario model omitted ₹8.4572 crore of opening current tax/employee/audit provisions, statutory liabilities and accrued interest; the ₹1.8034 crore capital-goods creditor was already in first-year capex and is not paid again. The revised model settles this once in year 1, without charging historical expenses or obtaining a second tax deduction. The company’s reported accounts are unchanged. [S1]

The current-claim correction does not quantify the separately disclosed unprovided gratuity obligation. No actuarial amount is available, so the model must not be read as establishing zero noncurrent employee liability; the existing financial-reliability hold remains. [S1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: A collection/markdown shock can turn reported profit into irrecoverable capital while supplier credit contracts. A20% inventory haircut is15.057cr,83.24% ofFY26 PAT;30additional collection days cost20.6126cr and withdrawal of10% supplier credit costs7.6175cr. These stresses are not interchangeable with additional sales. Failure to obtain equity or debt can force shrinking operations or adverse recapitalization. [S1]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold/tenfold price appreciation requires37.97%/58.49% annualized returns over five years. At unchanged current shares and an assumed15× exit PE,5×price requires188.5975cr PAT and10×377.1950cr versus18.0887cr, before incremental dilution; full proposed conversion raises share count23.52%. Such outcomes need extraordinary sustained cash growth, not bonus arithmetic or mere repeated invoicing. [S1] [S3] [S95]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: After23October verify actual vote and subsequent allotment,25% receipt and conversion separately. Request receivable bucket correction and post-year collections, stock ageing/returns/markdowns, supplier advances settlement and creditor terms. Track audit-trail remediation, auditor-transition documents, quarter-end bank returns and actual current cash/debt. Review each half-year result and immediately after material financing/credit events. [S1] [S3]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. Signed-note balance/provision uncertainty excludes ranking; persistent cash weakness remains independently observable. Linked models are counterfactual diagnostics, not investment targets. Resolve confirmations, quantify gratuity, verify collections/funding and establish executable liquidity before an implementation conclusion. [S1]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: IPO history and risks, FY24/FY25 reports, FY26 signed statements/controls,2024 resignation,2026 beneficial-owner corrigendum and future warrant notice reviewed. Secondary OHLCV is explicitly not official traded value. Model margins, recovery, financing availability and exit multiples are analyst assumptions; no scenario probabilities assigned. Missing current collections/stock realization prevent a confident fair-value conclusion. [S1] [S3] [S4] [S5] [S6] [S7] [S8] [S95]

GOV.reason: Persistent audit-trail weakness, rapid auditor/finance-team turnover and concentrated related financing merit below-average governance. Contrary evidence: explicit benign2024 resignation reason, current auditor says no outgoing objections, and financing ownership is disclosed. No misconduct inference.

MOAT.reason: Own brands/distribution have ordinary differentiation, but apparel trading has fashion risk, modest gross margin and no demonstrated durable pricing power. Lack of proven premium is evidence for an ordinary score, not automatic NS.

REV.reason: Substantial multi-year sales growth and expanding reported brand activity, offset by concentrated historical customers and receivables growing much faster than sales. Sell-through remains less certain than invoiced revenue.

DUR.reason: Broad apparel demand and distribution provide an ordinary reinvestment runway, but new working capital rather than manufacturing capacity is the bottleneck. Fashion and retailer-credit exposure constrain duration.

CAP.reason: CWIP/all-equity-inclusive capital proxy gives around20.6% average and22–23% incremental returns, but recoverability and increasing credit exposure warrant ordinary rather than premium capital-allocation quality. Signed notes disclose unquantified confirmation/provision effects; the numerical quality illustration is not a supported final factor pending quantification.

CASH.reason: Negative CFO in five consecutive historical years and a much larger current deficit after only one positive year demonstrate persistent cash-conversion weakness. FY25 positive cash is explicitly contrary evidence.

BAL.reason: Reported financial debt is modest relative to equity but supplier credit and inventory/receivable funding are substantial. Proposed equity cannot be counted as available cash; bear case requires unverified borrowing.

EXEC.reason: Management delivered higher sales, gross margin and core profit, but cash collection, outlet comparability and reporting controls lag the growth. Neither excellent execution nor complete absence of operating evidence is justified.

EARN.reason: FY26 earnings are mainly operating rather than other-income-driven, unlikeFY24. Removal of prior speculative losses also helps comparison; severe cash disconnect lowers quality. Signed notes disclose unquantified confirmation/provision effects; the numerical quality illustration is not a supported final factor pending quantification.
